coo_office.primary_setup: Your COO needs a short memo by tomorrow about a new way of planning that uses AI. You're thinking of letting an AI tool write the whole thing from last quarter's slides and old Slack messages.
coo_office.primary_stakes: If it names the wrong people, makes up numbers, or skips Legal and Finance, the whole leadership team will see it.
coo_office.complication_inject: Someone on your team pasted real customer details and private company goals into a shared ChatGPT chat while cleaning up the draft.
coo_office.standards_prompt: Think about the leaders who use AI to write memos and plans that other people then act on.

product.primary_setup: Your team wants to use an AI tool to write a product spec by Friday. The feature touches payments and needs a compliance check.
product.primary_stakes: If the requirements are wrong, or the AI makes up a policy detail, the launch could slip or need rework.
product.complication_inject: Someone on the team pasted real customer details into a shared ChatGPT chat while working on the spec.
product.standards_prompt: Think about how you'd set the quality bar when your team uses AI to write specs others will build from.

ops.primary_setup: An AI tool drafted a refund-and-apology reply for an upset VIP customer. A frontline agent wants to send it with one click.
ops.primary_stakes: The tone, the facts, and the policy all have to be right. A bad reply is public and hard to take back.
ops.complication_inject: The draft sounds kind, but it offers the wrong refund amount and promises an exception your policy doesn't allow.
ops.standards_prompt: Think about what agents can send on their own versus what they should pass up to someone else.

gtm.primary_setup: Marketing wants an AI tool to write a campaign email and landing page for a new product by tomorrow.
gtm.primary_stakes: The claims have to be true and brand-safe. Copy that sounds generic or off can hurt how people see you.
gtm.complication_inject: The draft includes a performance claim that's roughly true but hasn't been approved to use in public.
gtm.standards_prompt: Think about how brand, legal, and sales agree on what AI can draft and what stays human-written.

people.primary_setup: A manager wants to use an AI tool to draft a sensitive policy note and some talking points for managers.
people.primary_stakes: This affects employee trust. The wrong tone or a half-true summary of the policy can create real HR problems.
people.complication_inject: The AI confidently rewrites the policy in a way that sounds softer than the rule actually is.
people.standards_prompt: Think about who's allowed to use AI on people topics, who signs off, and what should never be pasted in.

risk.primary_title: A quick answer about your data
risk.primary_setup: A business partner asks for a quick AI-written summary of how your company handles data, for their vendor review.
risk.primary_stakes: Overstating what you do, or missing how long you keep data, can create audit and legal trouble.
risk.complication_inject: The AI draft says you delete all prompts within 24 hours. That isn't true for the tool your team actually uses.
risk.standards_prompt: Think about how you turn policy into simple rules people can actually follow day to day.

fin.primary_setup: You need a section of a board deck on the numbers. A colleague used an AI tool to draft the charts and the write-up from a spreadsheet.
fin.primary_stakes: A confident wrong number in a board pack is worse than a slide that's a little late.
fin.complication_inject: The AI mixed up two quarters in a growth chart, but the write-up still reads as if it's correct.
fin.standards_prompt: Think about the checks you'd want before any numbers or forecasts leave your desk.

gm.primary_setup: Leadership asks you to pick one AI project for the next six months: automating support, or improving forecasting. Both teams sent you business cases written by AI.
gm.primary_stakes: Money, risk, and attention are limited, and vendor demos often promise more than they deliver.
gm.complication_inject: One vendor's demo used made-up success numbers that don't match how your real data behaves.
gm.standards_prompt: Think about how you'd test a vendor's claims and decide when to stop a project before scaling it.
